body:
The LA Kings have promoted **Dr. John Meyer** to President of Player Health and Performance, **Jeff Andrews** to Head Athletic Trainer, **John Odgers** to Director of Performance and Sports Science, **Andre Carere** to Head Performance Coach, **Taylor Khoury** to Assistant Performance Coach, **Clayton Johns** to Assistant Equipment Manager, and **Paul Marino** to Senior Hockey Analyst - Lead Amateur and American Hockey League (AHL).

In addition, **Cassidy Papa** has been named Director of Rehabilitation, **Russ Romano** as Director of Player Care, **Brad Holland** as Pro Scout, **Elliott Kervin** as Data Scientist, and **Sean Maguire** as Emergency Backup Goaltender. **Steve Mastalerz** joined the organization last season as Goaltender Development Coach and Scout.

**Dr. John Meyer**

Dr. John Meyer has been named President of Player Health and Performance for the Kings, where he leads the organization’s comprehensive approach to player health, performance, injury prevention and rehabilitation. A clinician and leader in sports medicine and human performance, Dr. Meyer has practiced in the Los Angeles community for more than 25 years, specializing in biomechanical movement analysis and its relationship to orthopedic and sports injuries.

Dr. Meyer is also President and CEO of the Meyer Institute of Sport, based at Toyota Sports Performance Center in El Segundo. He and his team provide physical therapy, biomechanical movement analysis and preventative sports performance programs to the Kings and elite professional athletes across the NHL, NFL, NBA, PGA, MLB, UFC, USA Volleyball and Track and Field.

Previously, Dr. Meyer served as the Chairman of Performance Health and Wellness for the Los Angeles Clippers and Associate Athletic Director of Sports Science and Performance for the Department of Athletic Medicine at the University of Southern California. He has also served as an Adjunct Assistant Professor of Clinical Physical Therapy at USC, where his interests include spinal disorders, extremity injuries, movement science and sports performance. Dr. Meyer earned his Doctor of Physical Therapy degree and Orthopedic Residency Certificate from USC and is a Board-Certified Specialist in Orthopedics. 

**Jeff Andrews**

The fourth Head Athletic Trainer in LA Kings history, Andrews enters his sixth season with the organization, having joined as an Assistant Athletic Trainer in 2021. He has served in that role since joining the team’s training staff. Prior to joining the Kings, Andrews spent four seasons (2017-21) as Head Athletic Trainer for the Ontario Reign, the Kings’ American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate. He began his professional hockey career in athletic training as Head Athletic Trainer with the Elmira Jackals of the East Coast Hockey League (ECHL) before spending four season (2013-17) as Head Athletic Trainer with the Binghamton Senators (AHL) affiliate of Ottawa Senators.

A native of Horseheads, N.Y., Andrews earned his Bachelor of Science in Athletic Training from Alfred University in 2007 before receiving his Master of Science in Health Service Management from Elmira College in 2009. On March 30, 2025, Andrews worked his 1,000th career game in professional hockey.

**John Odgers**

Odgers is in his sixth season with the Kings, and first as Director of Performance and Sports Science. Since joining the organization in 2021, Odgers served in a Strength and Conditioning Coach capacity. Odgers joined the Kings after beginning his career in professional hockey with the Iowa Wild (AHL), where he served as the club’s Strength and Conditioning Coach.

Odgers’ interest in strength and conditioning developed during his junior hockey career, which included time with the Yorkton Terriers of the Saskatchewan Junior Hockey League (SJHL) and the Prince George Cougars of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He also completed a four-month internship with the San Jose Sharks while pursuing his graduate degree.

A native of Spy Hill, Saskatchewan, Odgers earned his bachelor’s degree in Kinesiology with a specialization in Human Kinetics and High Performance from the University of Regina in 2017 before completing his master’s degree in Kinesiology and Exercise Science from the same institution in 2019. In May of 2026, Odgers earned his Ph.D. in Sport Science from University of Lincoln. Odgers is the son of NHL veteran Jeff Odgers.

**Andre Carere**

Carere is set to begin his third season with the Kings, after spending the previous two seasons as the club’s Assistant Performance Coach. He joined the Kings following a two-year stint (2022-24) with the Ontario Reign (AHL), where he served as the team’s Head Strength and Conditioning Coach.

Carere began his professional hockey career with the AHL’s Springfield Thunderbirds, working as a Strength and Conditioning Intern during the 2021-22 season. That season, he was part of the Thunderbirds’ run to the 2022 Calder Cup Finals. His previous experience includes internships with the Calgary Flames, College of the Holy Cross and McMaster University. Carere served as a Graduate Assistant with Springfield College’s athletic department while completing his master’s degree in Strength and Conditioning. A native of Mississauga, Ontario, Carere earned his undergraduate degree in Kinesiology from Brock University in 2017.

**Clayton Johns**

Johns enters his first season with the Kings as an Assistant Equipment Manager, joining the organization after spending the last two seasons (2024-26) with the Ontario Reign. He originally joined the Reign as Head Equipment Manager following three seasons (2021-24) in the same role with the Portland Winterhawks of the Western Hockey League (WHL).

Prior to his time in Portland, Johns spent four seasons (2017-21) as Head Equipment Manager for the Barrie Colts of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). During the 2020-21 season, when the OHL did not play, he served as an Equipment Assistant with the Toronto Maple Leafs. Johns also spent two seasons as an Assistant Equipment Manager with the Oshawa Generals (OHL) and three years with the Carleton University men's hockey program.

**Paul Marino**

Marino is set to begin his fifth full season with the LA Kings’ Hockey Analytics Department, and first as Senior Hockey Analyst – Lead Amateur and AHL. Since joining the organization in March 2021 as a Statistical Analyst, Marino has held several roles within the department, most recently serving as a Hockey Analyst. Before joining the Kings, Marino spent four seasons with Harvard University’s Men’s Hockey Program as Assistant Director of Hockey Operations. During his time at Harvard, he supported the program’s hockey operations and analytics efforts while earning his bachelor’s degree in Statistics in 2020.

**Taylor Khoury**

Khoury joins the LA Kings organization as an Assistant Performance Coach for the 2026-27 season after spending the previous two seasons as the Head Strength and Conditioning Coach for the Ontario Reign.

Prior to joining the Reign, Khoury worked as a Sports Performance Coach at Mike Boyle Strength and Conditioning in Middleton, Massachusetts. During this time, he also served as a Strength and Conditioning Assistant at Merrimack College, working with the men’s and women’s hockey programs, as well as men’s basketball and track and field. Khoury also serves as the Lead Strength and Conditioning Coach for USA Hockey’s Men’s U17 Festival in New York, a position he has held for the past three years.

Khoury earned his bachelor’s degree in Kinesiology and Exercise Science from Merrimack College before completing a Master of Science in Strength, Conditioning, and Coaching Practice through Woolf University and the ALTIS Higher Education Program. A former defenseman, Khoury played collegiately at the NCAA Division III level at Manhattanville College and Hamline University after serving as captain of the Valley Jr. Warriors of the Eastern Hockey League (EHL).

**Cassidy Papa**

Cassidy Papa joins the Kings as Director of Rehabilitation after spending the previous two seasons as a physical therapist with the NBA’s Charlotte Hornets. Prior to joining Charlotte, she completed the Division I Sports Fellowship at Wake Forest University. She previously completed her sports residency at the University of Southern California and served as a physical therapist at the Meyer Institute of Sport, working under Kings Director of Player Health and Performance Dr. John Meyer.

Papa earned her Doctor of Physical Therapy degree from the University of Southern California after graduating from Stanford University with a bachelor’s degree in human biology. While at Stanford, she was a four-year member of the women’s water polo team. She is a Board-Certified Specialist in Sports and Orthopedic Physical Therapy and is a Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist.

**Russ Romano**

Romano joins the Kings after more than three decades with the University of Southern California, where he most recently served as Director of Operations of Athletic Medicine, Associate Athletic Director and Head Athletic Trainer. He originally joined USC in 1993 as an assistant athletic trainer, working with football and men’s basketball, before returning as Head Athletic Trainer in 1998.

Romano earned his bachelor’s degree in physical education with an emphasis in athletic training (1989) and master’s degree in physical education with an emphasis in biomechanics (1993) from San Diego State University. He later completed a fellowship in applied functional science at the Gray Institute of Functional Transformation and earned certification in Owens Recovery Science blood flow restriction.

At USC, Romano specialized in the care of Trojan student-athletes and contributed to research in sports medicine and rehabilitation. He is a principal member of the Keck School of Medicine of USC Neurorestoration Center and has served on the Pac-12 Brain Trauma Task Force. He received the 2019 Distinguished Alumnus Award from SDSU’s School of Exercise and Nutritional Sciences and was honored by USC with Marv Goux Award honors in August of 2026.

**Brad Holland**

Holland joins the Kings front office with nine years of experience in NHL hockey operations, including time with the Pittsburgh Penguins (2025), Edmonton Oilers (2019-24), Toronto Maple Leafs (2015-17) and NHL Hockey Operations. Most recently with Pittsburgh, Holland served a Hockey Operations Advisor. He previously held the role of Assistant General Manager and Director of Professional Scouting with Edmonton after being promoted from the club’s professional scouting department in July 2022. He originally joined the Oilers as a professional scout ahead of the 2019-20 season. Prior to joining Edmonton, Holland worked as a team manager with Toronto and held positions within the NHL’s Hockey Operations Department.

A graduate of Fordham University School of Law, Holland began his hockey career with the NHL in 2006, working in editorial and video roles before transitioning into league operations. He also practiced law before returning to hockey full-time, bringing a combination of analytical expertise and legal training to player evaluation and personnel decisions. During his tenure with Edmonton, Holland helped integrate data-driven analysis into the club’s scouting process and contributed to the evaluation of potential player acquisitions. Holland played collegiate hockey at Sacred Heart University before pursuing a career in hockey operations.

**Elliott Kervin**

Kervin joins the LA Kings’ Hockey Analytics Department after completing his Master of Data Science and Business Analytics at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte. A native of Orillia, Ontario, Kervin developed his skillset in hockey analytics through his graduate studies and mentorship from Dr. Michael Schuckers, leading to a research internship with the Kings focused on draft analytics.

During his time at UNC Charlotte, Kervin worked extensively in hockey analytics, including research into draft value, player evaluation and the use of natural language processing to quantify scouting reports. Kervin also gained recognition in the hockey analytics community by winning the Hackathon at the inaugural Hockey Analytics League Operations (HALO) Conference, where he used advanced data and artificial intelligence to explore player evaluation. Prior to his studies at UNC, Kervin earned his undergraduate degree in Accounting and Financial Management from the University of Waterloo.

**Sean Maguire**

Maguire begins his stint with the Kings as the team’s Emergency Backup Goaltender after serving as goalie coach for the University of New Hampshire men’s hockey program since 2023. He previously served as head instructor at Goaltending Development Services Inc. (GDS) in North Andover, Mass., founded by Kings goaltending coach Mike Buckley.

A native of Powell River, British Columbia, Maguire played two seasons (2010-12) for the Powell River Kings of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) before getting drafted by the Pittsburgh Penguins in the fourth round (113th overall) of the 2012 NHL Draft. Maguire played four seasons collegiate hockey at Boston University (2012-16) where he was named the 2016 Beanpot MVP in his senior year after making 65 of 67 saves over two games against Northeastern and Boston College.  He earned the Eberly Award for a tournament-best save percentage (SV%) of 0.970. He graduated holding the third-best career SV% in program history, establishing a .922 SV% in 62 games, which still stands today.

Maguire signed an entry level contract (ELC) with Pittsburgh in 2016 and continued into the professional ranks, playing three seasons of professional hockey, including three campaigns with the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins of the American Hockey League (AHL), while also seeing action with the Wheeling Nailers, Fort Wayne Komets and Utah Grizzlies of the East Coast Hockey League (ECHL). Maguire served as a black ace with the Penguins during their 2017 Stanley Cup Championship run.

**Steve Mastalerz**

Mastalerz joined the Kings as Goaltender Development Coach and Scout last season, bringing more than a decade of experience working with goaltenders at the professional, collegiate and youth levels. He previously served as Director of Player Development at the University of Massachusetts from 2023-25, returning to his alma mater after serving as a goaltending coach with the Manchester Monarchs from 2016-18.

Mastalerz began his coaching career in 2015 as a vice president and head instructor with Mike Buckley’s Goaltending Development Services and as goaltending coach for the Northeast Generals of the North American Hockey League.

Prior to coaching, Mastalerz played four seasons at UMass from 2011-15 before signing with the Manchester Monarchs, the Kings’ American Hockey League affiliate, following his senior season. A native of North Andover, Mass., he earned a bachelor’s degree in psychology from UMass in 2015. He also set the program’s Division I single-game saves record with 75 stops against Notre Dame in the 2015 Hockey East Tournament.

body:
The LA Kings have signed forward **Jared Wright** to a two-year contract extension worth an average annual value (AAV) of $925,000 through the 2028-29 season.

Wright, 23, tallied three points (2-1=3) in two games with the Ontario Reign this season, the Kings’ American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate, including the game-winning goal in Ontario’s season-opening win over Coachella Valley. Wright was recalled to the Kings on October 9.

Selected by the Kings in the sixth round (169th overall) of the 2022 NHL Draft, Wright made his NHL debut with the Kings on March 2 of last season and notched four points (0-4=4) in 23 games, including his first career point on March 7 against Montreal. He appeared in four postseason games as part of his Stanely Cup Playoffs debut. Wright also played in 54 games for the Reign, posting 17 goals and 30 points (17-13=30) with five game-winning goals, the second-most on the team.

The 6-1, 180-pound forward has suited up in 59 career AHL regular-season contests with Ontario over parts of three seasons, accumulating 19 goals and 34 points (19-15=34) with six game-winning goals, two shorthanded goals and 104 shots. He has one helper (0-1=1) in seven career Calder Cup Playoff outings.

Prior to his professional debut, Wright played three seasons of collegiate hockey at the University of Denver (NCHC), where he registered 32 goals and 54 points (32-33=54) in 122 games. In his sophomore year (2023-24), Wright collected 25 points (15-10=25) in a season that featured a career-long six-game point streak (Nov. 3-19, 2023; 4-3=7) capped by netting the game-winning goal in the NCAA Championship Game against Boston College on April 13, 2024, leading Denver to their 10th national title.

In addition to his National Championship, Wright earned several accolades during his time at Denver, including named to the NCHC Academic All-Conference Team twice (2022-23, 2023-24), chosen twice as a NCHC Distinguished Scholar-Athlete (2022-23, 2023-24), and winning two DU’s Dr. Ken Bredesen Most Sportsmanlike Player (2022-23, 2023-24) awards.

A native of Burnsville, Minn., Wright previously spent one season (2021-22) with the Omaha Lancers in the United States Hockey League (USHL), notching 34 points (15-19=34) in 59 regular-season games and three points (1-2=3) in four Clark Cup Playoff appearances. He finished third on the Lancers in scoring in his lone season and was named the team's rookie of the year.

body:
The LA Kings will retire **Anze Kopitar**’s No. 11 and unveil a bronze statue of the franchise’s all-time leading scorer at Crypto.com Arena on February 24, 2027, against the Montreal Canadiens. The ceremony represents the organization’s highest individual honor.

The all-time games played (1,521), assists (864) and points (1,316) leader in franchise history, Kopitar will become the eighth Kings player to have their number retired. Kopitar will join **Rogie Vachon** (#30), **Marcel Dionne** (#16), **Dave Taylor** (#18), **Wayne Gretzky** (#99), **Luc Robitaille** (#20), **Rob Blake** (#4) and **Dustin Brown** (#23) as part of the illustrious group of players to receive the honor. The statue outside Crypto.com Arena will be the fourth Kings statue with Kopitar joining Gretzky, Robitaille and Brown, along with broadcaster **Bob Miller** (who has a banner as well).

"To have my number retired and a statue unveiled by the LA Kings is an incredible honor, and one that is difficult to put into words," said Kopitar. "When I arrived in Los Angeles 21 years ago, I simply hoped to earn the opportunity to play in the NHL. I never imagined something like this. I have been fortunate to spend my entire career with one organization, surrounded by amazing teammates, coaches, staff and fans who have made this journey so special. I share this honor with everyone who has been part of it, especially my family, whose love and support have meant everything to me. I am truly grateful to be recognized in this way by an organization that has given me so much."

Tickets for February 24th can be secured now with a Season Ticket Membership or 6-game mini plan by visiting [lakings.com](https://www.nhl.com/kings/tickets/memberships/). Additional information on single game tickets will be released at a later date.

"Anze Kopitar has defined what it means to be a Los Angeles King for the past two decades,” said Luc Robitaille, LA Kings President. “His leadership, consistency and commitment to excellence have helped shape the identity of our franchise, both on and off the ice. He has earned the respect of everyone who has had the opportunity to play with him, coach him or watch him compete. Anze's legacy extends far beyond the records, awards and championships. He has inspired generations of Kings fans and left an indelible mark on our franchise, and the Los Angeles and Southern California community. We look forward to celebrating Anze, Ines and their family on what will be an unforgettable day in Kings history."

Kopitar, 38, recently completed his 20th – and final – NHL season, all with the Kings, where he accumulated 1,316 points (452-864=1,316) across 1,521 regular-season games, the most in franchise history. Kopitar’s 1,521 regular-season games are the 23rd-most in league history and the seventh-most played with a single franchise.

On March 14, 2026 in New Jersey, Kopitar was crowned as the all-time leading scorer in Kings history by posting his 1,307th and 1,308th career points. With his pair of goals in that game, Kopitar broke the record that had been held by **Marcel Dionne** (550-757=1,307) for more than 45 years. In doing so, he became the eighth player to hold the title. Just over a week prior, on March 5, Kopitar was the 25th different player in league history to skate in 1,500 career games and the ninth to do so with a single franchise.

The Jesenice, Slovenia native, ranks in the top-three of nearly every regular-season statistical category in Kings history, including first in seasons played (20), games played (1,521), assists (864), even-strength points (831), game-winning goals (79), overtime points (34) and face-off wins (15,237); second in plus/minus (+127), power-play points (457), overtime goals (9) and shots (3,429); third in goals (452), even-strength goals (309) and power-play goals (129).

He has led the Kings in points 15 times (most recently in 2022-23), the third-most seasons as points leader for one franchise in NHL history behind only **Gordie Howe** (17x w/ DET) and **Sidney Crosby** (16x w/ PIT). The trio are also three of only four players in league history to have at least 15 seasons as any team’s points leader, along with **Wayne Gretzky** (19x total; 9x w/ EDM, 7x w/ LAK, 3x w/ NYR). Kopitar (15x), Dionne (9x) and Gretzky (7x) make up the top-three on that list for Kings franchise history.

Selected 11th overall in the 2005 NHL Draft, Kopitar scored his first two career goals in his NHL debut on Oct. 6, 2006 in Anaheim. He went on to collect four more points over the next two games to become just second Kings player to record six points within the first three games of his career, and only the then-22nd to do so in NHL history. After positing 13 points during the month of October, Kopitar finished his rookie season with 61 points (20-41-61) in 72 games. He became the fifth rookie in team history – and the first in 20 years – to record 60 points in a season. No Kings rookie has reached that mark since. The following season (2007-08) marked the first of Kopitar’s 15 seasons leading the team in scoring with 77 points (32-45=77). He was named alternate captain prior to the 2008-09 campaign.

After earning his first NHL All-Star selection in 2008, Anze Kopitar emerged as the face of the Kings franchise, helping lead Los Angeles back to the Stanley Cup Playoffs in 2010 after an eight-year absence. He delivered several of the biggest goals of his career in the postseason, including overtime winners in the 2010 First Round and Game 1 of the 2012 Stanley Cup Final, while establishing himself as one of the NHL's premier two-way centers and faceoff specialists.

Named the Kings captain in 2016, Kopitar became synonymous with leadership, sportsmanship and consistency. He led the team to six Stanley Cup Playoff appearances (2018, 2021-26) during his time as captain, including each of the final five seasons of his career. In addition to the numerous regular-season records, Kopitar also owns many of the franchise’s playoff records, including games played (1st; 107), goals (3rd; 27), assists (2nd; 62), points (t-2nd; 89), game-winning goals (t-2nd; 5) and power-play points (3rd; 30).

Kopitar’s trophy case includes two Stanley Cup rings (2012 & 2014), two Selke Trophies (2015-16 & 2017-18), three Lady Byng Memorial Trophies (2015-16, 2022-23 & 2024-25) and the Mark Messier NHL Leadership Award (2021-22). Only Wayne Gretzky (7) has earned more individual NHL Awards while playing with the Kings than Kopitar (6).

Among team awards, Kopitar has earned 25 different team honors, including the Bill Libby Award for “Most Valuable Player” nine times (2007-08, 2009-10, 2010-11, 2013-14, 2015-16, 2017-18, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2022-23), Best Defensive Player eight times (2010-11, 2012-13, 2013-14, 2014-15, 2017-18, 2022-23, 2023-24, 2025-26), the Ace Bailey Memorial Award for “Most Inspirational Player” four times (2019-20, 2020-21, 2024-25, 2025-26), Most Popular Player three times (2006-07, 2010-11, 2020-21) and the Mark Bavis Memorial Award for “Best Newcomer” in 2006-07.

Beyond his accomplishments on the ice, Kopitar made a lasting impact throughout the Los Angeles community as a longtime supporter of Children's Hospital Los Angeles and the Make-A-Wish Foundation. He also played a leading role in growing youth hockey across Southern California through his continued involvement with the Kings and local hockey initiatives.

Kopitar’s bronze statue is being created by renowned sculptors Omri Amrany and Sean Bell. It will join statues honoring **Wayne Gretzky**, **Luc Robitaille**, **Dustin Brown**, **Bob Miller**, **Earvin "Magic" Johnson**, **Oscar De La Hoya**, **Chick Hearn**, **Jerry West**, **Kareem Abdul-Jabbar**, **Shaquille O'Neal**, **Elgin Baylor**, **Kobe Bryant**, **Kobe and Gigi Bryant**, and **Pat Riley** in Crypto.com Arena's Star Plaza along Chick Hearn Court.

The LA Kings will conduct a ribbon-cutting ceremony to commemorate the installation of a new LA Kings Hall of Fame at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, October 6 at 6 p.m. PT, in advance of their 2026-27 season home opener vs Florida at 7 p.m. The new permanent structure, located on the building’s main concourse adjacent to the Team LA store, celebrates the individual legacies and contributions of notable players, staff, and broadcasters from throughout the first 60 years of Kings history.

This museum display will include artifacts from the team’s 60-year history, plaques honoring each of the individual members of the Hall of Fame, and a new interactive set for fans to take photos alongside the likenesses of team icons from throughout the Kings’ storied past.

The existing class of the LA Kings Hall of Fame is highlighted by several players whose numbers currently hang in the rafters of Crypto.com Arena, including six former team captains and six members of the Hockey Hall of Fame. These individuals have been honored and recognized throughout the years as members of the Kings Hall of Fame and will now be permanently memorialized in this new structure.  The full class of members is as follows:

*   Rob Blake    
*   Dustin Brown    
*   Peter Demers (Trainer)
*   Marcel Dionne   
*   Wayne Gretzky    
*   Butch Goring
*   Anze Kopitar
*   Bob Miller (Broadcaster)
*   Luc Robitaille     
*   Dave Taylor   
*   Rogie Vachon

Artifacts and memorabilia on display will rotate on a regular basis, showcasing the Kings’ extensive archival collections in partnership with Heritage Werks Inc. and the Hockey Hall of Fame. Initial items on display include pucks from **Luc Robitaille**’s record-setting goal and final hat trick, **Dave Taylor**’s game-used stick from his 300th career goal, letters from President **Barack Obama** to the Kings, and more.

In addition to the Hall of Fame, the LA Kings announced that they will be creating a Hall of Fame Selection Committee.  This committee will be announced at a later date but will include a chairman and a board of members comprised of former players, executives, broadcasters, employees, and members of local television, radio and print media, all of whom have covered the team on an annual basis.

The committee will establish a criteria for membership consideration and will meet annually to consider new inductees each year.  Among the criteria for consideration are career statistics, playoff performance, longevity and consistency, legacy and off-ice contributions, team contributions, and league and team awards and recognition.

Further details regarding the Selection Committee will be released at a later date.

LA Skating Academy, the learn-to-skate program at Toyota Sports Performance Center (TSPC), the official practice facility of the LA Kings, has been recognized by Learn to Skate USA® for an outstanding 2025-26 season. The program earned a No. 1 national ranking and four program awards after growing to 5,155 members, giving thousands of Southern Californians their first step onto the ice.

LA Skating Academy grew from 3,536 members in 2024-25 to 5,155 in 2025-26, an increase of nearly 46 percent. That growth reflects Toyota Sports Performance Center's commitment to making skating accessible in a region where many residents have never laced up a pair of skates.

Learn to Skate USA awards in this category are reserved for programs that operate as part of a larger rink system, offering Learn to Skate USA classes at multiple ice rink locations. LA Skating Academy's work across multiple facilities distinguished it as one of the top programs in the country.

**2025-26 Season Highlights:**

*   **No. 1 national ranking** from Learn to Skate USA
*   **5,155 total members**, up from 3,536 the previous season
*   **Top 10 Multi-Facility Program** nationally
*   **Top 5 Multi-Facility Program** in the Pacific Section
*   **25%+ Year-over-Year Membership Growth** award
*   **Over 5,000 Members** award

"Every skater's journey begins with a first step onto the ice, and your programs serve as that entry point for hundreds of individuals and families in your community," Learn to Skate USA wrote in its recognition letter. "Through your dedication to creating a welcoming and engaging environment, you are helping more people experience the joy, confidence, and lifelong benefits that skating provides."\\

"Growing the game in Southern California starts with getting people comfortable on skates,” said **Chris Crotty**, General Manager of TSPC. “Toyota Sports Performance Center is where that happens every day, and this recognition shows how many families in our community are discovering the sport."

LA Skating Academy offers learn-to-skate programming for all ages and skill levels, serving as an entry point to figure skating, hockey and recreational skating. Registration information for upcoming sessions is available at [ToyotaSportsPerformanceCenter.com](http://toyotasportsperformancecenter.com/).

Toyota Sports Performance Center is operated by American Sports Entertainment Company (ASEC). ASEC is the leading independent owner/operator of ice skating and indoor sports facilities in the United States.

**NEW YORK** – New York Rangers left wing <forge-entity title="Alexis Lafreniere" slug="alexis-lafreniere-8482109" code="player">Alexis Lafreniere</forge-entity>, Dallas Stars goaltender <forge-entity title="Jake Oettinger" slug="jake-oettinger-8479979" code="player">Jake Oettinger</forge-entity> and St. Louis Blues right wing <forge-entity title="Jimmy Snuggerud" slug="jimmy-snuggerud-8483516" code="player">Jimmy Snuggerud</forge-entity> have been named the NHL’s “Three Stars” presented by GEICO for the week ending March 15.

## **FIRST STAR – ALEXIS LAFRENIÈRE, LW, NEW YORK RANGERS**

Lafrenière led the NHL with 5-2—7, highlighted by a pair of game-winning goals, in four contests to propel the Rangers (28-30-8, 64 points) to a perfect week. He notched 1-1—2, including the decisive tally, in a 6-2 triumph over the Philadelphia Flyers March 9. Lafrenière then recorded his second career hat trick, featuring his 24th career game-winning goal (and team-leading fifth of the campaign), in a 4-0 victory against the Calgary Flames March 10. He added 1-1—2, including an assist on the tiebreaking goal, in a 6-3 decision versus the Winnipeg Jets March 12 before being held off the scoresheet in a 4-2 win over the Minnesota Wild March 14. The 24-year-old Lafrenière, who has 9-6—15 in 11 contests since Jan. 31, has compiled 19-25—44 in 66 total games this season.

## **SECOND STAR – JAKE OETTINGER, G, DALLAS STARS**

Oettinger went 3-0-0 with a 1.65 goals-against average and .940 save percentage to help the Stars (42-14-10, 94 points) extend their point streak to a franchise record-tying 15 games dating to Jan. 23 (14-0-1) as they moved within three points of the Colorado Avalanche (44-12-9, 97 points) in the Presidents’ Trophy race. Oettinger denied 26 of 27 shots in a 2-1 win against the Vegas Golden Knights March 10. He then made 30 saves in a 7-2 triumph over the Edmonton Oilers March 12, followed by 22 stops in a 3-2 overtime victory against the Detroit Red Wings March 14. The 27-year-old Oettinger, who owns a 12-game point streak dating to Jan. 20 (11-0-1), ranks third in the NHL with 28 wins in 43 total appearances this season (28-10-5, 2.62 GAA, .900 SV%, 2 SO).

## **THIRD STAR – JIMMY SNUGGERUD, RW, ST. LOUIS BLUES**

Snuggerud registered 3-3—6 in four outings to power the Blues (27-30-10, 64 points) to a 2-1-1 week. He notched his first career three-point game with 1-2—3 in a 4-3 overtime loss to the New York Islanders March 10. Snuggerud then posted his second career multi-goal performance with a pair of tallies, including the game-winner, in a 3-1 decision versus the Carolina Hurricanes March 12. He was held off the scoresheet in a 3-2 overtime victory against the Edmonton Oilers March 13, but rebounded with one assist in a 3-2 loss to the Winnipeg Jets March 15. The 21-year-old Snuggerud sits fourth among rookies with 15-20—35 in 55 total contests this season, aided by a rookie-best 8-12—20 in 16 games since Jan. 24.

As the presenting partner of the NHL’s “Three Stars,” GEICO also is proud to celebrate the League’s “Fourth Star” – the fans whose dedication defines the sport. In [the latest episode](https://www.nhl.com/video/topic/4th-star/2025-26-nhl-fourth-star-champagne-family-6390437921112) of the “Fourth Star” series we follow **Seth** and **Krew Champagne**, a father and son who traveled to Tampa to watch the Boston Bruins play in the 2026 NHL Stadium Series, turning their shared love of hockey into a once-in-a-lifetime memory.

***DENVER*** - The National Hockey League announced this evening that Colorado Avalanche left wing **Gabriel Landeskog** was selected as the winner of both the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy and the Mark Messier Leadership Award for the 2025-26 season. Landeskog becomes the first player in NHL history to win both awards over his career, which also makes him the first ever to capture both in the same season.

The Masterton Trophy is awarded to the player who best exemplifies the qualities of perseverance, sportsmanship and dedication to hockey. A $2,500 grant from the Professional Hockey Writers Association (PHWA) is awarded to the Bill Masterton Scholarship fund each year in the name of the winner. The Messier Award is given to the player who exemplifies great leadership qualities to his team, on and off the ice, during the regular season and who plays a leading role in his community growing the game of hockey.

Landeskog, 33, was nominated for the Masterton by the local chapters of the PHWA for his perseverance in returning to the Avalanche after missing the 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular seasons. In 2025-26, the Avalanche captain recorded 35 points (14g/21a) in 60 regular-season contests and added 11 points (6g/5a) over 13 Stanley Cup Playoff games to rank second on the team in goals. Colorado, which won the 2025-26 Presidents’ Trophy, compiled a 45-7-8 regular-season record when Landeskog dressed and a 10-9-3 record when he did not.

A native of Stockholm, Sweden, Landeskog completed his 14th season as the Avalanche’s team captain and is the third-longest tenured captain in the NHL behind Sidney Crosby (19 seasons) and Alex Ovechkin (17 seasons). He entered 2025-26 tied for the seventh-longest tenured captain in NHL history. In addition to his Avalanche leadership duties, Landeskog was the captain for Team Sweden at the 2026 Winter Olympic Games, the first Olympics with NHL players since 2014. He chipped in four points (2g/2a) over five showings in Milan.

Off the ice, Landeskog’s community involvement included speaking at Kroenke Sports and Entertainment’s (KSE) Charity Brunch in March, spearheading the team’s annual hospital visit and hosting numerous local foundations through the Avalanche organization’s Community Ticket Pride program. Some of the foundations include, but are not limited to, the National Sports Center for the Disabled, Vitalant Blood Donations, Juvenile Assessment Center (JAC), and over 20 schools in the state of Colorado.

Landeskog played in Game 3 of the 2025 First Round (April 23, 2025) after not playing for 1,032 days since his last contest in Game 6 of the 2022 Stanley Cup Final (June 26, 2022) due to multiple knee surgeries. He's just the third captain ever to go over 1,000 days between NHL games along with Sid Abel (Detroit, 1,045 days) and Syl Apps (Toronto, 1,009).

Following the Avalanche capturing the Stanley Cup on June 26, 2022, Landeskog missed the entire 2022-23 season following knee surgery, then underwent cartilage transplant surgery on May 10, 2023 that cost him the entire 2023-24 campaign as well as all of the 2024-25 regular season. After years of rehabilitation, Landeskog appeared in two AHL games for the Colorado Eagles as a part of a conditioning stint on April 11-12, 2025. In five 2025 NHL playoff contests upon his return, Landeskog registered four points (1g/3a). Both times he found the scoresheet were multi-point outings that led to Avalanche victories. As part of Landeskog’s quest to return to the Avalanche’s lineup, the forward chronicled his rehab work in a six-part documentary series titled “A Clean Sheet.”

In addition to recovering from knee procedures, Landeskog had two separate stints of missing games due to injury in 2025-26. He was out of the lineup for 14 games due to an upper-body injury from Jan. 6 – Feb. 4 and seven more due to a lower-body injury from March 8-20.

Landeskog is the first player in Avalanche/Nordiques history to earn either award. The Masterton Trophy was established in 1967-68, and the Mark Messier Leadership Award debuted in 2006-07. Nominee suggestions for the latter are solicited from fans, clubs and NHL personnel, but the selection of the winner is chosen by Messier.

body: **NEW YORK (May 4, 2026)** – Buffalo Sabres defenseman **Rasmus Dahlin**, Colorado Avalanche forward **Gabriel Landeskog** and Winnipeg Jets forward **Jonathan Toews** are the three finalists for the 2025-26 Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy, which is awarded “to the player who best exemplifies the qualities of perseverance, sportsmanship and dedication to hockey,” the National Hockey League announced today. The local chapters of the Professional Hockey Writers Association (PHWA) submitted nominations for the Masterton Trophy at the conclusion of the regular season and the top three vote-getters were designated as finalists. **Gabriel Landeskog, Colorado Avalanche** Landeskog missed three full regular seasons with knee issues after playing through injury during the Avalanche’s 2022 Stanley Cup run. He had four major procedures done, including knee cartilage replacement surgery in May 2023. He became the first player ever to return to the NHL after having that procedure done when he re-joined the Avalanche during the 2025 playoffs. If his comeback wasn’t remarkable enough, his first full season back included broken ribs after crashing into the net in January. “I don’t know if there’s a mode, but if you can go on NHL26 and build the captain, you just copy Gabe Landeskog,” [Avalanche forward Parker Kelly told Corey Masisak](https://www.denverpost.com/2026/04/23/one-year-later-avalanche-captain-gabe-landeskog-very-pleasantly-surprised-with-how-his-body-has-held-up/) in the *Denver Post.* “That’s what you’re going to build. He has it all, man. Just feel super lucky to play with him and super happy for him to get back in the lineup, do as well as he’s done this year, making an impact every night.” The Presidents’ Trophy-winning Avalanche went 45-7-8 when Landeskog was in the lineup and 10-9-3 when he was not. **Bill Masterton Memorial Scholarship Fund** A $2,500 grant from the PHWA is awarded annually to the Bill Masterton Scholarship Fund, based in Bloomington, Minn., in the name of the Masterton Trophy winner. **History** The trophy was presented by the NHL Writers’ Association in 1968 to commemorate the late **Bill Masterton**, a player with the Minnesota North Stars who exhibited to a high degree the qualities of perseverance, sportsmanship and dedication to hockey and who died on Jan. 15, 1968. **Announcement Schedule** The series of NHL Trophy finalist announcements continues Tuesday, May 5, when the three finalists for the **Calder Memorial Trophy** will be unveiled.

**BROSSARD, Quebec --** Martin St. Louis blew his whistle at the end of practice and ordered <forge-entity title="Lane Hutson" slug="lane-hutson-8483457" code="player">Lane Hutson</forge-entity> to go take an extra lap.

The Montreal Canadiens defenseman happily obeyed his coach's order, skating with his typical ease, but there was an element of freedom in each stride. Financial freedom, to be sure, but also a freedom from worry.

While Hutson circled the ice, St. Louis announced to the rest of the team that the 21-year-old signed an eight-year, $70.8 million contract with the Canadiens on Monday.

"As a hockey player, the ice is our sanctuary," St. Louis said. "At the end of practice, I had the chance to have all my players in the same place. It's pretty rare that I can get everyone together without having to call a team meeting. I'm not surprised by the players' reaction. I like that, almost more than a win."

<forge-entity title="Cole Caufield" slug="cole-caufield-8481540" code="player">Cole Caufield</forge-entity> jumped into Hutson's arms at the end of the lap. The rest of the Canadiens quickly followed, swarming Hutson behind the net, the reaction resembled that of a team that had just won a game in overtime in the Stanley Cup Playoffs.

"That was a pretty cool and special moment," Hutson said. "That's just the group we have, pretty tight knit."

"Lane was happy to take that lap," said St. Louis with a smile. "He loves to skate."

On the eve of the Canadiens' home opener against the Seattle Kraken at Bell Centre on Tuesday, general manager Kent Hughes and team president Jeff Gorton wrapped up one of the team's most pressing business matters.

"We were hoping to get it done before the start of the year, but we got there after three games," Hughes said.

Hutson won the Calder Trophy, awarded annually to the top rookie in the NHL, with 66 points (six goals, 60 assists) last season, becoming just the seventh player in Canadiens history to receive the honor and first since the late <forge-entity title="Ken Dryden" slug="ken-dryden-8446490" code="player">Ken Dryden</forge-entity>, who won the award in 1972. His 60 assists tied an NHL rookie record set by <forge-entity title="Larry Murphy" slug="larry-murphy-8449745" code="player">Larry Murphy</forge-entity> with the Los Angeles Kings in 1980-81.

Hutson's new contract, which begins with the 2026-27 season, has an average annual value of $8.85 million through 2033-34. He has one assist in three games this season.

"I tried not to let myself get distracted by the negotiations, but it was starting to weigh on me a little," he said. "It's a good thing for both sides to come to a deal. I'm just happy to be here for a long time.

"I think every time you get to throw on this jersey, it's special, whether it's practice, games, preseason, playoffs. It always means so much to me, and it's pretty special that I get to do it for a while now."

Hutson and his agent, Ryan Barnes of Quartexx Management, sped up the negotiation process with the Canadiens at the start of October. He said that terms were essentially finalized before a 3-2 win against the Chicago Blackhawks at United Center on Saturday.

"It's been hard to read the market lately," Hughes said. "When a player like <forge-entity title="Connor McDavid" slug="connor-mcdavid-8478402" code="player">Connor McDavid</forge-entity> [signs a contract](https://www.nhl.com/news/connor-mcdavid-signs-2-year-deal-with-edmonton) (two years, $25 million, $12.5 million AAV with the Edmonton Oilers) for far less than another player in the League (<forge-entity title="Kirill Kaprizov" slug="kirill-kaprizov-8478864" code="player">Kirill Kaprizov</forge-entity>; [eight years, $136 million, $17 million AAV](https://www.nhl.com/news/kirill-kaprizov-signs-eight-year-136-million-contract-with-minnesota-wild) with the Minnesota Wild), it's a big reminder that there's a salary cap.

"With this contract, Lane just told us that he likes playing in Montreal and that he wants the Canadiens to be in a position to win. We're very happy to keep him here with us. We were also really happy to have drafted him as late as we did (second round, No. 62 in the 2022 NHL Draft). We've lucky to have him here with us, and to have him here on a long-term basis."

Much like Caufield, <forge-entity title="Nick Suzuki" slug="nick-suzuki-8480018" code="player">Nick Suzuki</forge-entity> and <forge-entity title="Juraj Slafkovsky" slug="juraj-slafkovsky-8483515" code="player">Juraj Slafkovsky</forge-entity>, Hutson chose to accept an eight-year contract with Montreal immediately following his rookie deal, avoiding a massive burden on the team's salary structure.

"I like seeing a teammate get a nice salary, one that's to the level of his talent, but we've kind of built a culture here where guys are not trying to break the bank," Suzuki said. "I think all Lane wants to do is win, and I think he's definitely set us up for that possibility moving on in the future."

Hughes stayed true to his personal philosophy, convincing Hutson to accept a yearly salary that respects the team's cap space, rather than seek out what could have been a higher wage on the open market.

"It was a priority for us," Hughes said. "When the salary cap changes, the numbers are no longer the same, but our principles have to remain the same."

Hutson will earn slightly less than teammate <forge-entity title="Noah Dobson" slug="noah-dobson-8480865" code="player">Noah Dobson</forge-entity>, who signed an eight-year, $76 million contract ($9.5 million AAV) with the Canadiens after he was acquired in a trade with the New York Islanders on June 27.

"Noah's was a different contract," Hughes said. "The contracts for 'Suzie,' Caufield, 'Slaf,' Kaiden Guhle and Lane are all contracts following their NHL rookie deals. This one's different.

"We talked about our desire to build a winning culture. That's important for us. To get there, everyone's got to be pulling in the same direction."

**NEW YORK** – Montreal Canadiens defenseman <forge-entity title="Lane Hutson" slug="lane-hutson-8483457" code="player">Lane Hutson</forge-entity>, who shared the rookie lead with 13 points in 14 games (2-11—13), has been named the NHL’s “Rookie of the Month” for December.

Hutson edged San Jose Sharks center <forge-entity title="Macklin Celebrini" slug="macklin-celebrini-8484801" code="player">Macklin Celebrini</forge-entity> (4-9—13 in 13 GP), Philadelphia Flyers right wing <forge-entity title="Matvei Michkov" slug="matvei-michkov-8484387" code="player">Matvei Michkov</forge-entity> (3-7—10 in 13 GP), Canadiens teammate <forge-entity title="Emil Heineman" slug="emil-heineman-8482476" code="player">Emil Heineman</forge-entity> (4-5—9 in 14 GP) and Calgary Flames goaltender <forge-entity title="Dustin Wolf" slug="dustin-wolf-8481692" code="player">Dustin Wolf</forge-entity> (4-1-1, 2.64 GAA, .905 SV%, 1 SO) for the honor.

Hutson also paced December rookies in assists (11), power-play assists (7), power-play points (7), average time on ice (21:18) and total time on ice (298:07). Only one rookie defenseman has recorded more assists or points for Montreal in a single calendar month: **Chris Chelios**, in both February 1985 (1‑14—15 in 12 GP) and December 1984 (1-13—14 in 15 GP).

Hutson found the score sheet in 10 of his 14 December appearances, producing two point streaks of five games: Dec. 1-9 (0-6—6) and Dec. 14-23 (2-5—7). The former extended his overall assist/point streak to seven contests (Nov. 27 – Dec. 9: 0-8—8), the longest by a rookie defenseman in franchise history ahead of **Glen Harmon** (Jan. 9-19, 1943: 2-5—7 in 6 GP) and Chelios (Dec. 16-27, 1984: 1-8—9 in 6 GP and March 1-14, 1985: 3-6—9 in 6 GP).

The 20-year-old Hutson, a second-round pick (62nd overall) from the 2022 NHL Draft, places third among rookies – behind only Michkov (12-17—29 in 36 GP) and Celebrini (12-15—27 in 28 GP) – with 2-24—26 through 37 total contests this season. He also ranks among the top rookies in assists (1st; 24), power-play assists (1st; 11), blocked shots (1st; 47), takeaways (1st; 17), average time on ice (1st; 22:26), total time on ice (1st; 830:10), power-play points (2nd; 11) and shots on goal (t-11th; 42).

Hutson follows Michkov (October: 4-5—9 in 11 GP) and Celebrini (November: 7-5—12 in 14 GP) as a “Rookie of the Month” winner in 2024-25. He is the first Canadiens player to receive the honor since current teammate <forge-entity title="Cole Caufield" slug="cole-caufield-8481540" code="player">Cole Caufield</forge-entity> in March 2022 (7-8—15 in 15 GP).

**NEW YORK** – Montreal Canadiens defenseman <forge-entity title="Lane Hutson" slug="lane-hutson-8483457" code="player">Lane Hutson</forge-entity>, who paced all rookies with 14 assists and 15 points in 14 games (1-14—15) to lift the Canadiens (34-30-9, 77 points) into the final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference, has been named the NHL’s “Rookie of the Month” for March.

Hutson edged Philadelphia Flyers right wing **Matvei Michkov** (5-9—14 in 16 GP), Anaheim Ducks left wing **Cutter Gauthier** (3-10—13 in 15 GP), St. Louis Blues center **Zack Bolduc** (8-3—11 in 15 GP), and San Jose Sharks teammates **Will Smith** (4-7—11 in 13 GP) and **Macklin Celebrini** (3-8—11 in 13 GP) for the honor.

Hutson, who previously was named [“Rookie of the Month” for December](https://media.nhl.com/public/news/18520), joins Michkov (October and February) as a repeat winner this season. He is the first defenseman to earn the honor multiple times within the same campaign since **Nicklas Lidstrom** in 1991-92 (November and December w/ DET) and the first Canadiens player *at any position* with multiple “Rookie of the Month” recognitions in the same season since center **Kjell Dahlin** in 1985-86 (October and December).

Hutson, a second-round pick (62nd overall) in the 2022 NHL Draft, became the first rookie defenseman with at least 14 assists in a single calendar month since **Alexei Zhitnik** in March 1993 (5‑14—19 in 14 GP w/ LAK). Only two other rookie blueliners since Zhitnik have compiled at least 15 points in a single calendar month: **Cale Makar** in November 2019 (7-9—16 in 14 GP w/ COL) and **Quinn Hughes** in February 2020 (2-13—15 in 13 GP w/ VAN).

Hutson additionally ranked among the top three March rookie skaters in total time on ice (1st; 327:08), average time on ice (1st; 23:22), power-play assists (1st; 6), power-play points (t-1st; 6), even-strength assists (3rd; 8), even-strength points (3rd; 9) and plus/minus (t-3rd; +7).

He found the score sheet in nine of his 14 March appearances, including five multi-assist/point performances and his second career three-assist game (March 30 at FLA). His 14 total multi-assist efforts in 2024-25 are tied for the second-most in a season by a rookie blueliner in NHL history, behind just **Chris Chelios** in 1984-85 (16 w/ MTL).

The 21-year-old Hutson tops all rookies, forwards and defensemen, with 5-54—59 through 73 overall contests in 2024-25. He also leads rookies in assists (54), total time on ice (1,651:16), average time on ice (22:37), even-strength assists (30), power-play assists (24) and power-play points (25).

Only two rookie defensemen in League history have accumulated more assists in a single campaign: **Larry Murphy** in 1980-81 (60 w/ LAK) and Chelios in 1984-85 (55 w/ MTL). Hutson also is [one of 10 rookie blueliners](https://www.nhl.com/stats/skaters?aggregate=0&reportType=season&seasonFrom=19171918&seasonTo=20242025&gameType=2&position=D&isRookie=1&filter=points,gte,59&sort=points,goals,assists&page=0&pageSize=50) in NHL history with at least 59 points in a season – and the first since Lidstrom in 1991-92 (11-49—60 w/ DET).

<forge-entity title="Lane Hutson" slug="lane-hutson-8483457" code="player">Lane Hutson</forge-entity> signed an eight-year, $70.8 million contract with the Montreal Canadiens on Monday. It has an average annual value of $8.85 million and begins next season.

The 21-year-old defenseman could have been a restricted free agent after this season.

"Nice to get a good bit of business done," Hutson said. "For me, it's back to work and building my game. I think it's good for both sides. I'm just happy to be here for a long time."

Hutson was voted winner of the Calder Trophy last season, given to the NHL rookie of the year after his 66 points (six goals, 60 assists) in 82 games broke <forge-entity title="Chris Chelios" slug="chris-chelios-8446053" code="player">Chris Chelios</forge-entity>' Canadiens record (64 in 1984-85) for most by a first-year defenseman. His 60 assists tied an NHL rookie record from a defenseman set by <forge-entity title="Larry Murphy" slug="larry-murphy-8449745" code="player">Larry Murphy</forge-entity> in 1980-81 and he was Montreal's second Calder winner in the expansion era (since 1967-68) after goalie <forge-entity title="Ken Dryden" slug="ken-dryden-8446490" code="player">Ken Dryden</forge-entity> (1971-72).

"I had a conversation with Lane over the weekend and he had talked about his view on things," Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes said. "It struck me he wanted to make sure we understood how much he wanted to be here and how hard he was going to work. I kind of cut him off and said, 'Lane, there wouldn't be an eight-year deal if we didn't believe in who you were at your core.' The kind of person he is, how committed he is to being his best version of himself, but also being the best version of a teammate.

"That's important to us. One of the things that we've talked a lot about is trying to build a culture here and a culture where everybody's pulling in the right direction, and that's absolutely critical in my opinion."

A second-round pick (No. 62) in the 2022 NHL Draft, Hutson has one assist in three games this season, and 69 points (six goals, 63 assists) in 87 regular-season games. He has five assists in five Stanley Cup Playoff games, when they lost the Eastern Conference First Round to the Washington Capitals, and helped the Canadiens make the postseason for the first time since they advanced to the 2021 Stanley Cup Final, a five-game loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning.

"I think every time you get to throw on this jersey, it's special, whether it's practice, games, preseason, playoffs," Hutson said. "It always means so much to me, and it's pretty special I get to do it for a while now. I have belief that we aren't far off from being a team that can be a Stanley Cup championship team, and not just once. Hopefully we continue to do it, but the belief I have in this group, the staff, coaches, everything we have in place, I think we're heading in a great direction. I just really trust what we're doing here."

The Canadiens play their home opener against the Seattle Kraken at Bell Centre on Tuesday (7 p.m. ET; RDS, TSN2, KONG, KHN) after going 2-1-0 on a season-opening three-game road trip.

"The reality is, if you go out into the open market, you're going to have to pay," Hughes said. "Our hope is that we're able to build this team as much as possible internally, but if ... when you have a young group of players that are committed to this team, I think we owe it to them that if we believe there's a hole in the lineup that's needed to be filled in order to have a championship-caliber team, then we're going to have to do that."

<forge-entity title="Lars Eller" slug="lars-eller-8474189" code="player">Lars Eller</forge-entity> signed a one-year, $1.25 million contract with the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday.

The 36-year-old forward had 22 points (10 goals, 12 assists) in 80 regular-season games for the Washington Capitals and Pittsburgh Penguins including 15 points (six goals, nine assists) in 63 games with Washington after he was acquired in a trade on Nov. 12.

Eller had one assist in nine Stanley Cup Playoff games.

"I'll definitely keep playing. My body feels good, so I'm going to keep playing," Eller said on Capitals' break up day on May 17.

Selected by the St. Louis Blues with the No. 13 pick in the 2007 NHL Draft, Eller has 424 points (118 goals, 236 assists) in 1,116 regular-season games for the Blues, Montreal Canadiens, Colorado Avalanche, Penguins and Capitals and 50 points (15 goals, 35 assists) in 112 playoff games.

He won the Stanley Cup with the Capitals in 2018.

The Senators also signed forward <forge-entity title="Nick Cousins" slug="nick-cousins-8476393" code="player">Nick Cousins</forge-entity> to a one-year, $825,000 contract.

The 31-year-old forward had 15 points (six goals, nine assists) in 50 games last season. He won the Stanley Cup with the Florida Panthers in 2024

*NHL.com senior writer Tom Gulitti contributed to this report*

Laurent Brossoit and Vladislav Namestnikov each signed a contract with the Winnipeg Jets on Saturday.

Brossoit, a goalie, signed a one-year, $1.75 million contract; Namestnikov, a forward, signed a two, year, $4 million contract ($2 million AAV).

Brossoit was 7-0-3 with a 2.17 goals-against average and .927 save percentage in 11 regular-season games (10 starts) for the Vegas Golden Knights last season. The 30-year-old was 5-2 with a 3.18 GAA and .894 save percentage in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. He did not play after sustaining a lower-body injury in Game 3 of the Western Conference Second Round against the Edmonton Oilers; the Golden Knights went on to win the Stanley Cup.

"It was one of those injuries that my timeline didn't really allow me an opportunity to play again," Brossoit said. "But in that last series, I could have gone on the ice and started working through that, but we just felt it wasn't necessary. So the health is good, I'm in a lot better position than I was last year at this time, so I'm very excited."

Selected by the Calgary Flames in the sixth round (No. 164) of the 2011 NHL Draft, Brossoit is 49-41-11 with a 2.78 GAA, .908 save percentage and three shutouts in 117 regular-season games (96 starts) for the Golden Knights, Jets and Edmonton Oilers and 5-2 with a 3.26 GAA and .888 save percentage in nine playoff games (eight starts).

"Obviously we have some depth on the back end right now, that will have to sort itself out as we go here," Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said. "In net, we have a strong tandem there. I'm excited about this group."

***[RELATED: [NHL Free Agent tracker](https://www.nhl.com/news/free-agency-signings-2023/c-344949384?tid=281072352)]***

Namestnikov had 25 points (eight goals, 17 assists) in 77 regular-season games for the Jets and Tampa Bay Lightning last season. The 30-year-old had 15 points (six goals, nine assists) in 57 games until he was traded to the San Jose Sharks for forward <forge-entity title="Michael Eyssimont" slug="michael-eyssimont-8479591" code="player">Michael Eyssimont</forge-entity> on March 1, 2023. Two days later, he was sent to the Jets for a fourth-round pick in the 2024 NHL Draft

He had two assists in five playoff games.

Selected by the Lightning in the first round (No. 27) of the 2011 NHL Draft, Namestnikov has 261 points (115 goals, 146 assists) in 630 regular-season games for the Jets, Lightning, Dallas Stars, Detroit Red Wings, Colorado Avalanche, Ottawa Senators and New York Rangers and 13 points (six goals, seven assists) in 53 playoff games.

Goalie <forge-entity title="Collin Delia" slug="collin-delia-8480420" code="player">Collin Delia</forge-entity> also signed a one-year, $775,000 contract with the Jets on Saturday. He was 10-6-2 with a 3.28 GAA and .882 save percentage in 20 games (18 starts) for the Vancouver Canucks last season. The 29-year-old is 19-18-7 with a 3.51 GAA and .897 save percentage in 52 regular-season games (45 starts).

The Jets traded forward <forge-entity title="Pierre-Luc Dubois" slug="pierre-luc-dubois-8479400" code="player">Pierre-Luc Dubois</forge-entity> to the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday for forwards <forge-entity title="Gabriel Vilardi" slug="gabriel-vilardi-8480014" code="player">Gabriel Vilardi</forge-entity>, <forge-entity title="Alex Iafallo" slug="alex-iafallo-8480113" code="player">Alex Iafallo</forge-entity>, and <forge-entity title="Rasmus Kupari" slug="rasmus-kupari-8480845" code="player">Rasmus Kupari</forge-entity>, and a second-round pick in the 2024 NHL Draft.

"The keeping of 'Vladdy', the addition of the three forwards, I think it really gives us a group of forwards that we really haven't had at any point in time in this organization from top to bottom," Cheveldayoff said. "That group of 12, 13, or 14 forwards there, there are lots of options, there are lots of ways to put them together."

Forward Blake Wheeler had the final season of his five-year, $41.25 million contract bought out by the Jets on Saturday.

"You look at the moves we made, obviously, the PLD trade was something that worked exactly how we hoped it might," Cheveldayoff said. "You never know going into something like that if it can. You addressed some of your needs right now. You get a good pick in next year's draft.

"I do want to say that I would like to extend my most heartfelt thank you to Blake Wheeler and his family for all of the years that he put into this organization, what the family has put into the community and the player that he was. He bet on us several times and, unfortunately, we got close but just not close enough. He was a tremendous part of that."

The Jets (46-33-3) lost to the Golden Knights in five games in the first round of the playoffs last season.

body:
**FAIRFIELD, Conn. --** <forge-entity title="Frank Vatrano" slug="frank-vatrano-8478366" code="player">Frank Vatrano</forge-entity> is still beaming three weeks after the Anaheim Ducks decided to match the offer sheet <forge-entity title="Leo Carlsson" slug="leo-carlsson-8484153" code="player">Leo Carlsson</forge-entity> signed with the Philadelphia Flyers.

Vatrano, taking part in the fourth annual edition of the [Shoulder Check Showcase](https://www.nhl.com/news/shoulder-check-showcase-continues-to-grow-raise-mental-health-awareness) at Sacred Heart University, admitted on Thursday to some nervous moments during the time when Carlsson was tendered the five-year, $90 million offer sheet ($18 million average annual value).

The veteran Ducks forward admits he couldn’t imagine the on-the-rise Ducks without their 21-year-old star-in-waiting occupying the middle of the ice.

“I think for him to come in this year completely healthy and experiencing that play in the playoffs at the highest level, it will only help him,” Vatrano said. “Obviously, when you get that kind of contract, you're going to be playing with confidence.

“You always play with confidence, but for him, it’s another step. He wants to be that guy. You can see he's a great kid. Yeah, I could definitely see him taking a huge, huge step this season.”

Carlsson was named to Team Sweden for the 2026 Winter Olympics but missed the tournament because of injury. Yet, Vatrano says that honor, as well as Carlsson’s selection to play for Sweden at the 2025 4 Nations Face-Off turbocharged the player’s confidence.

“He was around all those guys and, you know, that's a big thing in anybody's career, but especially that young,” Vatrano said. “I mean, I even noticed it, but I think even at the (4 Nations), I think you noticed a completely different player when he came back.

“Just him going there and being around all those guys. He took that huge step and even after the Olympics this year, I know he would have loved to be there. He’s the player that we all thought he was going to be.”

Carlsson was second on the team during the regular season with 67 points (29 goals, 38 assists) in 70 games, behind forward <forge-entity title="Cutter Gauthier" slug="cutter-gauthier-8483445" code="player">Cutter Gauthier</forge-entity> (69 points), and tied with forward Troy Terry for second during the postseason with 11 points (four goals, seven assists) in 12 games.

Last season was the first time a Ducks team reached the Stanley Cup Playoffs since 2018.

Carlsson is Anaheim's No. 1 center, offensively adept with top-end speed, who plays a 200-foot game that coach Joel Quenneville can feel comfortable matching against the opposition's top lines.

“I think that if you've watched our games the last couple years, I think Leo's first two years, we weren't, we weren't the best team, so he wasn't getting the numbers that maybe were warranted and what he deserved,” said Ducks forward <forge-entity title="Sam Colangelo" slug="sam-colangelo-8482118" code="player">Sam Colangelo</forge-entity>, who was also at the Shoulder Check event. “This year, the start of the year, he was leading the League in points or top-three, and faced some injuries and it was kind of tough.

“I think that if people watch our games closely, they know that Leo's a 100-point player and there's no doubt about that. And he's also a different player. If you watch him play, he does it all. Plays a top-line matchup. He can defend, he wins face-offs, he creates. He's a hell of a player and I'm excited to watch him continue to grow.”

The Ducks are growing with Carlsson, who general manager Pat Verbeek called the “cornerstone piece” of the franchise when he [matched the offer sheet](https://www.nhl.com/news/topic/free-agency/leo-carlsson-signs-5-year-contract-with-ducks-match-flyers-offer-sheet) on July 9.

The Ducks were 43-33-6 last season and finished third in the Pacific Division, a point behind the Edmonton Oilers, who they defeated in six games in the first round. Carlsson was used in matchups against two of the best forwards in the League in <forge-entity title="Connor McDavid" slug="connor-mcdavid-8478402" code="player">Connor McDavid</forge-entity> and <forge-entity title="Leon Draisaitl" slug="leon-draisaitl-8477934" code="player">Leon Draisaitl</forge-entity> in that series and more than held his own.

In the next round, Anaheim lost in six games to the Vegas Golden Knights, who were the Western Conference representative in the Stanley Cup Final, losing to the Carolina Hurricanes in six games.

There are so many young players around Carlsson in the lineup.

Forward <forge-entity title="Beckett Sennecke" slug="beckett-sennecke-8484762" code="player">Beckett Sennecke</forge-entity> is 20. Gauthier and defenseman <forge-entity title="Pavel Mintyukov" slug="pavel-mintyukov-8483490" code="player">Pavel Mintyukov</forge-entity> are 22. Colangelo is 24. Franchise defenseman <forge-entity title="Jackson LaCombe" slug="jackson-lacombe-8481605" code="player">Jackson LaCombe</forge-entity>, who played for the United States at the Olympics, is 25.

“I think we have a lot of young guys who took a lot of big steps this year,” said Colangelo, who was limited to nine games with the Ducks last season, but had 36 points (12 goals, 24 assists) in 49 games with San Diego of the American Hockey League. “I'm looking to kind of get back on track and get back to how I played my rookie year.

“And I think that our team's going to continue to get better. I mean, obviously we lost some key pieces, but I think that some young guys are ready to take the next step.”

That means the playoffs are the goal again this season. No one-and-done for these Ducks, says Vatrano.

“Just because we did it one year doesn't mean you're going to be back next year, so for us, it doesn't get much easier,” he said. “No, we're going to have a target knowing that we're a good team. So we're going to get the best from every team every single night. Every team's going to get better, and we got to get better too.”

body: Is Leo Carlsson really an $18 million per year player? Did the Philadelphia Flyers do the right thing by signing the Anaheim Ducks center to an offer sheet that will pay him that much for the next five seasons, equaling $90 million in the 21-year-old's pocket? There are wide-ranging opinions about the Flyers decision to offer sheet Carlsson, how it impacts his future and the rest of the NHL, and what the Ducks should do now with a deadline of Friday to either match or refuse and accept the four first-round draft picks as compensation. This week's episode of the "[NHL @TheRink](https://www.nhl.com/multimedia/podcasts/nhl-therink)" podcast tackles the topic and all the tentacles that come off the Carlsson contract with co-hosts Dan Rosen and Shawn P. Roarke providing their thoughts and -- you guessed it -- differing opinions on what's at stake. For a primer, just know that Rosen is in love with what the Flyers did and the guts it takes, and he believes Carlsson is worth every penny, but Roarke is lukewarm on it and gives some dissenting takes that make sense. In addition to Carlsson's offer sheet, the podcast dives into the situation with Zach Werenski and the Columbus Blue Jackets, with the co-hosts discussing why it's a tough spot for the team and how it seems as though a big decision is being punted down the road. They also hit on Alex Ovechkin re-signing with the Washington Capitals for his 22nd season and the challenge ahead for coach Spencer Carbery.  The co-hosts take issue with the Toronto Maple Leafs signing Sergei Bobrovsky to a three-year contract and discuss the Edmonton Oilers signing goalie Frederik Andersen to a one-year contract. The episode will be the last before a summer hiatus, though Rosen and Roarke could check in before September if big news warrants it. The "[NHL @TheRink](https://www.nhl.com/multimedia/podcasts/nhl-therink)" podcast is free and listeners can subscribe on all podcast platforms. It is also available on [NHL.com/multimedia/podcasts](https://www.nhl.com/multimedia/podcasts/) and the NHL app.

body:
**LAS VEGAS –** <forge-entity title="Leo Carlsson" slug="leo-carlsson-8484153" code="player">Leo Carlsson</forge-entity> isn’t feeling any pressure despite owning one of the richest contracts in the NHL.

The forward signed a five-year, $90 million contract ($18 million average annual value) on July 9 with the Anaheim Ducks, who matched the offer sheet the Philadelphia Flyers tendered to Carlsson on July 3.

A lot of expectations come with that but for Carlsson, it’s just par for the course.

“There’s been pressure all the time since I got into the League,” he said at the NHL/NHLPA North American Player Media Tour at City National Arena on Wednesday. “Getting drafted second overall (in the 2023 NHL Draft), some people thought I shouldn’t. There’s obviously a little more pressure now but it’s nothing that I can’t handle.”

Yes, Carlsson is confident. So are the Ducks, who qualified for the Stanley Cup Playoffs last year for the first time since 2017-18. Anaheim was eliminated by the Vegas Golden Knights, who advanced to the Stanley Cup Final, in six games in the Western Conference Second Round.

Part of that confidence comes from defeating the Edmonton Oilers in six games in the first round. The Oilers had been to the Stanley Cup Final two straight seasons, losing to the Florida Panthers both times. It was a tough test facing the Oilers and two of the League’s best forwards in <forge-entity title="Connor McDavid" slug="connor-mcdavid-8478402" code="player">Connor McDavid</forge-entity> and <forge-entity title="Leon Draisaitl" slug="leon-draisaitl-8477934" code="player">Leon Draisaitl</forge-entity>, but the Ducks were up to it.

“We had a few guys that were really hard on them, too. <forge-entity title="Jackson LaCombe" slug="jackson-lacombe-8481605" code="player">Jackson LaCombe</forge-entity> played a huge, huge part in this series, just basically doing a great job of shutting down McDavid, which is probably the hardest job in the world,” Carlsson said. “We just had a perfect balance. It’s always hard to come into their place as well, the fans are screaming and the place is rocking.

“We should be really proud of what we did. It brings a lot of confidence to know that we can be a really, really good team and we can compete against the best.”

The 21-year-old is coming off his best NHL season, with career highs in goals (29), assists (38) and points (67) in 70 regular-season games and 11 points (four goals, seven assists) in 12 postseason games last season. When the Flyers tendered the offer sheet to Carlsson, he was the second player to get one this offseason after the New Jersey Devils signed forward <forge-entity title="Barrett Hayton" slug="barrett-hayton-8480849" code="player">Barrett Hayton</forge-entity> to a one-year, $4.775 million contract on July 1. The Utah Mammoth announced one week later that they were matching the contract.

For Carlsson, the whole thing was crazy.

“Yeah, because it was so unexpected, that’s why. I mean, (Cale) Makar, you know those guys are going to sign big contracts,” Carlsson said of the Colorado Avalanche defenseman, who signed an eight-year, $163.2 million contract with a League-record $20.4 million AAV on Aug. 28.

“We didn’t know (the Flyers) were going to offer sheet me like that. It’s special.”

And for a brief time, Carlsson was the highest paid player in the NHL.

“Yeah, we knew. My team knew it was going to be for a short time. It was fun for a while,” Carlsson said with a smile. “I’m not complaining at all.”

Now it’s on to this season and getting a playoff appearance streak going.

“The expectations are higher than last seasons were,” Carlsson said. “Our expectations are to make the playoffs again because we know we can do it.”

When the Flyers tendered the offer sheet to Carlsson, he was the second player to get one this offseason after the New Jersey Devils signed forward <forge-entity title="Barrett Hayton" slug="barrett-hayton-8480849" code="player">Barrett Hayton</forge-entity> to a one-year, $4.775 million contract on July 1. The Utah Mammoth announced one week later that they were matching the contract.

For Carlsson, the whole thing was crazy.

“Yeah, because it was so unexpected, that’s why. I mean, (Cale) Makar, you know those guys are going to sign big contracts,” Carlsson said of the Colorado Avalanche defenseman, who signed an eight-year, $163.2 million contract with a League-record $20.4 million AAV on Aug. 28.

“We didn’t know (the Flyers) were going to offer sheet me like that. It’s special.”

And for a brief time, Carlsson was the highest paid player in the NHL.

“Yeah, we knew. My team knew it was going to be for a short time. It was fun for a while,” Carlsson said with a smile. “I’m not complaining at all.”

Now it’s on to this season and getting a playoff appearance streak going.

“The expectations are higher than last seasons were,” Carlsson said. “Our expectations are to make the playoffs again because we know we can do it.”

title: Carlsson Ready to Deliver on Expectations

body:
<forge-entity title="Leo Carlsson" slug="leo-carlsson-8484153" code="player">Leo Carlsson</forge-entity> is staying with the Anaheim Ducks.

The center signed a five-year, $90 million contract with the Ducks on Thursday after they matched an offer sheet tendered to the 21-year-old center by the Philadelphia Flyers on July 3.

"It was kind of an offer that I think everyone would sign," Carlsson said. "When you see that number, it's hard to say no. ... My team, they understand, too, completely. They would have done the same thing."

The contract has an average annual value of $18 million, the richest in NHL history.

“We are very happy to have Leo under contract for five years,” Ducks general manager Pat Verbeek said. “We have viewed Leo as a franchise player since the moment we met him prior to the 2023 draft. He’s a character person on and off the ice. Leo is viewed as a top player in this league, and it was always our intention to match any offer sheet.”

Anaheim had until Friday to either match the offer sheet or allow Carlsson to join Philadelphia. If the Ducks had decided not to match the contract, they would have received four first-round draft picks from the Flyers as compensation.

"We understood this outcome was possible when we made the offer," Flyers general manager Daniel Briere said Friday. "While the result isn't what we hoped for, our goal does not change - we remain committed to pursuing every opportunity that will strengthen our team and continue to build towards becoming a consistent and perennial contender without sacrificing our future."

Carlsson set NHL career highs in goals (29), assists (38) and points (67) in 70 regular-season games for Anaheim last season. He also had 11 points (four goals, seven assists) in 12 Stanley Cup Playoff games.

"It was an offer that 99 percent of people would sign too," Carlsson said. "It's a pretty simple answer. I really wanted to be here, though. I really wanted them to match. I want to be an Anaheim Duck."

Selected by the Ducks with the No. 2 pick in the 2023 NHL Draft, Carlsson has 141 points (61 goals, 80 assists) in 201 regular-season games over three seasons. He completed a three-year, entry-level contract he signed on July 12, 2023. 

Carlsson was the second player to receive an offer sheet this offseason; on Wednesday, the Utah Mammoth [matched the one-year, $4.775 million contract](https://www.nhl.com/news/barrett-hayton-offer-sheet-matched-by-utah-mammoth) given to forward <forge-entity title="Barrett Hayton" slug="barrett-hayton-8480849" code="player">Barrett Hayton</forge-entity> by the New Jersey Devils on July 2.

“I think from the day that we drafted him, we viewed him as a cornerstone piece of our rebuild, and that hasn't changed,” Verbeek said. “Leo and I have a great relationship, and I think that this whole thing has been worked through. 

“My feelings for Leo hasn't changed since the day that we drafted him. We've got the business at hand taken care of, and just the both of us are looking forward to building off the season that we had last year, and towards winning a Stanley Cup.”

*NHL.com deputy managing editor Adam Kimelman contributed to this report*
